definitions.explanation: A strong feeling of wanting something or wishing for something to happen.

examples.japanese: {強|つよ}い{願望|がんぼう}を{持|も}つ。
{願望|がんぼう}を{叶|かな}えるために{努力|どりょく}する。
examples.english: I work hard to fulfill my wishes.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{留学|りゅうがく}は{長年|ながねん}の{願望|がんぼう}だった。
examples.english: Studying abroad was a long-held desire of mine.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}には{出世|しゅっせ}への{強|つよ}い{願望|がんぼう}がある。
examples.english: He has a strong desire for career advancement.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}からの{願望|がんぼう}がやっと{叶|かな}って、{自分|じぶん}の{店|みせ}を{開|ひら}くことができた。
examples.english: My childhood wish finally came true, and I was able to open my own shop.

notes:
{願望|がんぼう} refers to a deep, heartfelt wish or desire — something one earnestly hopes for. It carries a more personal and emotional tone than {希望|きぼう}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {願望|がんぼう}を{持|も}つ: to have a desire
- {願望|がんぼう}を{叶|かな}える: to fulfill a wish
- {強|つよ}い{願望|がんぼう}: strong desire
- {潜在的|せんざいてき}{願望|がんぼう}: latent/subconscious desire
- {長年|ながねん}の{願望|がんぼう}: a long-held desire

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {希望|きぼう}: hope, wish (more neutral and practical; used for requests and applications)
- {欲望|よくぼう}: desire, lust (often negative; implies greed or excessive want)
- {望|のぞ}み: wish, desire (literary and poetic)
- {願|ねが}い: wish, request (everyday; also used for prayers and formal requests)

REGISTER:
Slightly literary. More common in written language, psychology ({願望|がんぼう}{充足|じゅうそく} = wish fulfillment), and formal speech than in casual conversation.
